page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-64 is a high-memory compute instance equipped with 64 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture and 504.0 GB of system memory. This architecture yields approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, targeting workloads that require significant memory allocations relative to processing cores.

The instance does not include integrated local storage, meaning operating system persistence and storage I/O depend on external network-attached block volumes. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs allocated. Additionally, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly to the virtual machine.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio offers resource density for deployments constrained by RAM capacity rather than processing thread counts. Tradeoffs include reliance on networked storage for all disk operations and the lack of acceleration hardware. The c4d-highmem-64 instance is structured for in-memory databases, large-scale caching, extract-transform-load pipelines, and enterprise application backends requiring a dense memory footprint.
